topic: Constructors in C++: Initialization and Best Practices
explanation: Constructors are special member functions that initialize objects of a class.  They have the same name as the class and are automatically called when an object is created.  Effective use of constructors ensures proper object initialization, avoiding undefined behavior and improving code readability.  Different constructor signatures allow for flexible object creation based on available data.
example_explanation: The example demonstrates different constructor types: a default constructor (initializes members to default values), constructors taking string(s) and numerical arguments for explicit initialization and a constructor that reads data from an input stream.  This showcases flexible object creation based on context.  In-class initializers provide default values, improving code readability. The use of a constructor initializer list for members like `bookNo` ensures efficient initialization. The `main` function shows how to use each constructor to create different `Sales_data` objects, demonstrating practical real-world usage scenarios such as taking inputs from different sources.
